sections.body: A PRIMARY source was made at the time by someone who was there: a diary, a photo, a letter, an object.
A SECONDARY source was made later, about the past: a textbook, a documentary, an encyclopedia.
Historians use both, and ask: Who made it? When? Why? Could it be one-sided?

quiz.q: Which is a PRIMARY source about a 1950s school?
options: A photo taken in that school in 1955
hints: Primary sources come from the time itself.
Which one was made in the 1950s?
A soldier's letter written during a war is a primary source. Which option was made at the time?
quiz.explain: A photo taken in 1955 was made at the time, so it's primary.

quiz.q: Why should historians ask who made a source?
options: The maker might have a point of view or bias
hints: Could the maker want to show only one side?
A team's own website might only show their wins. Does that tell the whole story?
quiz.explain: Knowing who made it helps you spot a point of view or bias.

quiz.q: Which is a SECONDARY source about ancient Egypt?
options: A pot made in ancient Egypt
A letter written by an ancient Egyptian
hints: Secondary sources were made later, about the past.
Which one was made long after ancient Egypt ended?
Example: a diary written during a famous flood is a primary source. It was made at the time.
quiz.explain: The documentary was made thousands of years later, so it's secondary. The pot and letter are primary.
